results.summary: The audit of {META_ConfigurableSystem} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. All referencing design sections adhere to the definition of using header macros and constexpr for compile-time static determination of system parameters. Numeric values for JIT cache and memory limits are consistent across the architecture overview and detailed component specifications.

The audit of {META_3TierSeparation} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. All referencing design sections correctly implement the 3-tier decomposition (Tier 1: Primary, Tier 2: Decomposed Subcomponent, Tier 3: Leaf Component) as defined in the architecture specification. Dependency management via the harness pattern is consistently applied across the tiers to maintain the required encapsulation and zero-overhead goals.

The audit of {META_RecoveryStrategy} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The definition of replacing error codes with recovery strategies is uniformly implemented across the WIT interfaces, system services, and runtime components. The four defined strategies (ignore, retry, restart, panic) are consistently applied with matching preconditions and post-conditions across all referencing sections.

The audit of {GLOBAL_StaticScalability} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. All design sections adhere to the definition of eliminating dynamic overhead via compile-time constants. Numeric allocations for the minimum configuration are mathematically sound and consistent across the resource budget and system configuration details.

The audit of {META_BinarySearch} across all referencing design sections confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The definition of O(log N) search on sorted arrays is consistently applied across the JIT pipeline, system containers, and JIT runtime components. The 'Narrow-then-Search' optimization is logically integrated and substantiated by a concept implementation.

The audit of {FlatViewNarrowing} across all referencing design sections confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The implementation of the 'narrow-then-search' pattern is uniformly applied across JIT lookup, vMMIO access, and debugger breakpoint management.

The audit of the {IPCRouter} requirement across the provided design sections shows high vertical and horizontal consistency. All referencing components (System Logging, IPC Router, System Service, and Platform HAL) strictly adhere to the invariant that all system calls must pass through the IPC Router.

The audit of {META_FaultIsolation} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The definition of preventing fault propagation via memory partitioning is consistently implemented across the architecture (Heap Partitions), the system services (WASM isolation), the runtime (boundary checks), and the platform layer (MPU region allocation).

The specification for {RoleBasedAccessControl} is highly consistent across all definition and design sections. The static role matrix is defined concretely in the configuration and implemented consistently in the IPC router's lookup pipeline and sequence diagrams. The claim regarding deadlock prevention is backed by a specific verification artifact.

The audit of {OwnershipTransfer} confirms high vertical and horizontal consistency across the IPC Router, vMMIO, and Platform Memory sections. The design successfully decomposes the abstract definition into a concrete 3-stage handoff (Revoke -> Enqueue -> Grant) with robust error recovery (Rollback) and emergency cleanup (Drop Handler).

The audit of {GLOBAL_Policy_Memory} across all referencing design sections confirms strict adherence to the defined policy of prohibiting dynamic heap allocation (malloc/new) in favor of static or stack-based allocation.

The specification for {ThreadedInterpreter} is highly consistent across all architectural layers. The definition's requirements for __fastcall CPS, register-based variable holding, and JIT calling convention alignment are strictly implemented and detailed in the design sections.

The specification for {IPC_ZeroCopy} is highly consistent across all architectural layers. The definition of eliminating data copying is concretely implemented via a three-stage ownership transfer (Revoke -> Enqueue -> Grant) and supported by a dedicated static shared memory budget.

The audit of {GLOBAL_InterruptWakeup} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency across all architectural tiers. The design implements a decoupled 'push-pull' notification model that aligns with the requirement of waking up associated tasks without violating the cooperative multitasking constraints of the COOS.

The specification for {BufferedLogging} is consistent across all referencing design sections. The definition's requirement for ring-buffering and idle-time transfer is fully realized through the interaction between the system_logging component and the COOS idle hook.

The specification for {PackedBitView} is exhaustively consistent across all definition and design sections. The implementation details in the design sections strictly adhere to the constraints defined in the requirement list, and the provided conceptual Python code serves as a concrete artifact substantiating the architectural claims.

The audit of {JIT_RuntimeAPI_Fallback} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections correctly implement the requirement to offload complex instructions to runtime APIs to maintain JIT engine simplicity and a single-pass compilation path.

The audit of {META_StaticDI} across all referencing design sections confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The implementation of 'Static Dependency Injection' is consistently described as the use of POD structures (harnesses) to achieve dependency inversion without runtime overhead (vtable/virtual functions), aligning perfectly with the definition of compile-time static binding.

The audit of {META_RestrictedPhysicalAccess} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The definition of restricting physical resource access via permission tables is consistently implemented across the vMMIO configuration, the system call interface, and the runtime safety constraints.

The audit of {DictionaryBasedIPC} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The definition of reducing IPC transfer volume via static dictionary offsets is accurately implemented across the logging component and the IPC router interface.

The architectural policy for harness application is fully aligned across all tiers. Tier 1 COOS uses coos_harness for static internal component binding, Tier 2 Subsystems use vsoc_harness, while Tier 3 leaf components (such as jit_compiler) are confirmed to operate as single-responsibility units without redundant harnesses.

The audit of {GLOBAL_IndependentHeap} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency across all definition and design sections. The requirement for independent heap memory areas for fault isolation is consistently implemented through static partitioning of a consolidated physical pool.

The audit of {GLOBAL_PeriodicTask} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency across all referencing design sections. The definition is correctly implemented as a mechanism for periodic task scheduling, specifically utilized by the JIT compiler for background batch compilation and integrated into the COOS scheduler's idle handling logic.

The audit of {JIT_OldestOnly_Promote} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency across all referencing design sections. The promotion policy is consistently defined as 'Oldest-Only', and the supporting physical architecture (3-bank rotation) and memory budgets are mathematically aligned.

The specification for {CSP_Handoff} is highly consistent across all architectural layers. The definition's requirements for scheduler bypass, symmetric transfer, and bounded consecutive handoffs are strictly adhered to in the physical design, algorithm descriptions, state machines, and formal verification invariants.

The Resource_Estimation_Model requirement is consistently implemented across all referencing design sections. The definition's mandate to estimate ROM/RAM footprints and verify constraint suitability is concretely realized through a static assertion model in the system configuration and a budget tracking document.

The audit of {Type_Vocabulary} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections correctly implement the definition as a set of strict type aliases and vocabulary to link specifications and implementation across different architectural tiers.

The design explicitly integrates execution profiler sampling (hotspot PC sampling and frequency tracking) and dynamic test tool validation hooks into the DebugManager and RuntimeInterpreter, satisfying all requirements of {Debug_Integrated}.

The design sections for {ROMParsing} are strictly consistent with the definition. The implementation strategy (ModuleView, BinaryStream, and Accessors) directly realizes the 'Zero Copy Loading' requirement by referencing ROM data via spans and offsets rather than expanding the module into RAM.

The audit of {URIAbstraction} across the provided sections shows strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections correctly implement the URI-based abstraction for loose coupling and service discovery as defined in the requirements.

The audit of {Challenge_ApproximateYield} confirms full vertical and horizontal consistency across the definition and design sections. The transition from a 'Pending' (検討中) status in the requirement list to a 'Decided' (決定済) status in the ADR is correctly reflected in the implementation details of the runtime and vSoC engine.

The audit of {META_NoStdVector} across all referencing design sections confirms strict adherence to the prohibition of std::vector and dynamic memory allocation. All components consistently implement fixed-length arrays, static pools, or non-owning views.

The audit of {FastAddressCheck} across all definition and design sections confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The requirement for a single-instruction size comparison without masking is uniformly implemented across the JIT stencils, the vMMIO bypass logic, and the runtime environment structure.

The audit of {Challenge_IpcQueueStarvation} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections correctly implement the 'Rollback' mechanism defined as the mitigation for starvation in the definition section, and explicitly distinguish this bounded mailbox mechanism from the CSP Rendezvous mechanism to avoid conceptual confusion.

The audit of {MemoryIsolation} across the provided sections shows full vertical and horizontal consistency. All design sections correctly implement the definition's requirement for hardware or logical boundaries to ensure memory safety.

The specification for {VDMA} is consistent across all definition and design sections. The high-level requirement for high-speed transfer between guest linear memory and virtual/physical addresses is concretely implemented through a defined register set, a clear execution algorithm, and integration with the system's interrupt and memory management (TLB) systems.

The specification for {IPC_DropHandler} is consistent across all definition and design sections. The design correctly implements the requirement for in-flight resource recovery to prevent leaks, with a clear mapping from the high-level definition to the state machine and formal verification properties.

The design sections for {MultiModule_Support} are vertically and horizontally consistent with the definition. The requirement for multiple module loading and dynamic linking is fully addressed through the implementation of a Module Registry and a defined dynamic linking sequence.
The specification for {Debugger_Jit_Flush} is exhaustive, consistent across all architectural layers, and backed by formal verification artifacts.

The audit of {GLOBAL_UseCpp20Coroutine} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections correctly implement the requirement for C++20/23 coroutines, specifically detailing the use of Symmetric Transfer to achieve the low-overhead context switching goals defined in the requirements.

The audit of {ADR_RendezvousChannel} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency across all referencing design sections. The definition of a bufferless synchronous rendezvous is consistently applied across the physical design, core OS data structures, state transition tables, and scheduler logic. A critical distinction is explicitly maintained between the CSP Rendezvous Channel and the IPC Router's bounded mailboxes, preventing architectural confusion.

The audit of {TypeSafeMessaging} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency across all referencing design sections. The implementation details in the IPC Router and HAL sections align perfectly with the definition's requirements for type safety, search efficiency (O(log N)), and the use of fireball::flat_map_view.

The design sections are strictly consistent with the definition of {CooperativeMultitasking}. The implementation details regarding C++23 coroutines, symmetric transfer for low overhead, and the integration with the system call interface (SYS_YIELD) and IRQ flags align perfectly across all referenced documents.

The specification for {CSPCommunication} is highly consistent across all referenced design sections. The definition of Hoare CSP, zero-copy ownership transfer, and the rendezvous mechanism is strictly maintained from the high-level requirements through to the conceptual implementation and the system call interface.

The design sections are strictly consistent with the definition of {Asynchronous_Notification}. The implementation strategy correctly bridges the high-level WASI 'pollable' requirement with the low-level vSoC virtual interrupt mechanism.

The audit of {RSPMinimalSet} confirms vertical and horizontal consistency across the definition and referencing design sections. The design correctly implements the 'minimal set' constraint by delegating the detailed command specification to a single source of truth (the GDB RSP Physical Specification) and distributing the implementation responsibilities across the HAL (parsing) and Debug Manager (execution) without contradiction.

The specification for {JIT_Safepoint} is consistent across all definition and design sections. The design provides concrete implementation details (loop-back edges, interrupt flags, and state transitions) that align with the high-level definition. Formal verification claims are properly backed by specific model file references.
The specification for {Challenge_JITCacheEfficiency} is highly consistent across all architectural layers, from high-level ADRs to detailed buffer layouts and formal verification properties.

The design sections are strictly consistent with the definition of {NativeAPI_Export}. The implementation details regarding the single trap instruction and vMMIO register usage are coherently distributed across architectural and runtime layers without contradiction.

The requirement {RSP_Transport_Selectable} is consistently implemented across all referencing design sections. The definition's mandate for selectable transport layers is explicitly realized in the HAL layer with specific support for UART and RTT, and is correctly referenced as a conceptual dependency in the Debug Manager and RSP Parser.

The requirement {Interpreter_LazyJITSwitch} is consistently implemented across the definition and design sections. The mechanism for re-evaluating the JIT cache during loop returns is explicitly detailed in the runtime interpreter algorithm and supported by the system sequence diagrams.

The specification for {LightweightVerifier} is consistent across all referencing sections. The definition of a 'fast verifier performing minimal checks' is correctly implemented in the design as a set of specific checks (magic value, version, section boundaries) and is properly integrated into the loader's state machine and backlog.

The audit of {vMMIO_TrapAndEmulate} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections correctly implement the requirement to trap guest memory accesses and invoke host hooks, with a unified boundary check mechanism shared across the JIT and Interpreter paths.

The audit of {WasmPageAlignment} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency across all referencing design sections. The definition of 64KB page alignment is consistently applied from the high-level requirement down to the physical memory layout and MPU configuration.

The design sections for {JIT_Encoder} are strictly consistent with the definition. The use of C++ constexpr for build-time instruction template generation is uniformly implemented across RISC-V and ARM architectures and correctly integrated into the JIT Compiler's decomposition.
The HAL interface correctly defines standard IPC abstractions, buffer management, and verified fast-path mechanisms. Traceability links and return mappings are completely defined and compliant.

The audit of {Challenge_InterruptSafety} confirms full vertical and horizontal consistency across the definition and design sections. The implementation strategy evolves logically from a high-level goal to a specific mechanism.

The keyword {META_AI_Native_Dev} is consistently used as a traceability marker across design and planning documents, aligning with its definition of leveraging LLMs for implementation while focusing on design/verification quality. However, a traceability gap was detected in one technical section.

results.summary: The audit of {META_SpecificationFirst} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections correctly implement the 'specification-first' stance by establishing formal models, WIT contracts, and a rigorous quality gate before proceeding to implementation.

The audit of {META_BumpAllocator} across the definition and referencing design sections shows full consistency. The designs correctly apply the allocator's purpose (preventing fragmentation and providing high-speed allocation) and extend it with specific implementation details (LIFO constraints and transaction rollback) that are compatible with the nature of a bump allocator.

The design sections for {Trap_Interface} are strictly consistent with the definition and with each other. The documentation correctly distinguishes between the trap-based synchronous interface and the vMMIO direct-store fast path, avoiding any conceptual contradiction.

The design sections strictly adhere to the definition of {Errorcode_To_Strategy}. The transition from low-level errno (Syscall) to high-level recovery strategies (WIT) is consistently described across the system call and interface layers.

The implementation of {WASI_Implementation} is consistent across the definition and design sections. The architecture correctly separates the low-level syscall mapping (Tier 1 Core) from the high-level WIT interface definitions (Tier 1 Interface), maintaining a clear layered perspective without redundant duplication.

The audit of {Syscall_Mapping} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections correctly implement the static mapping of WASM guest instructions to host syscall IDs as defined in the requirements.

The audit of {Fast_Path_GPIO} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections correctly distinguish between the high-performance vMMIO direct-store path and the portable Shim/HAL paths, adhering to the definition's requirement for a bypass of the abstraction layer.

The design sections strictly adhere to the definition of {ZeroCopyIndexing}. The implementation details in the runtime loader align with the high-level requirement of avoiding RAM copies for WASM sections and strings.

The audit of {PhysicalPassthrough} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The definition of a high-speed path bypassing memory copies is correctly implemented across the vMMIO runtime and HAL layers.

The design sections strictly adhere to the definition of {TaskPollInterruptFlag}, maintaining a clear separation between the push-based notification (ISR to Queue) and pull-based observation (Guest Engine Safepoint).

The design sections strictly adhere to the {CleanArchitecture} requirement. The dependency direction is explicitly defined as 'Inner' (Kernel) and 'Outer' (Subsystem/Hardware), with a clear prohibition of Inner-to-Outer #include dependencies. This is consistently reflected in the BDD diagram where the Subsystem Layer 'realizes' interfaces defined by the Kernel Layer (IPC Router), effectively implementing the Dependency Inversion Principle.
Zero overhead properties are substantiated with benchmark artifacts and constexpr static dispatch in accordance with project standards.

The audit of {META_Risk_Tiering} confirms that the keyword is consistently applied across architecture principles, project management phases, and quality gates. The design sections correctly utilize the definition of 'risk-based design layering' to justify the prioritization of formal verification for high-risk components.

The audit of {META_CompileTimeValidation} across the provided sections shows full consistency. The definition's requirement for static type checking and constexpr-based error detection is strictly implemented in the design sections through the use of static_assert and constexpr DSLs.

The specification for {DirectContextSwitch} is consistent across all definition and design sections. The design correctly implements the requirement of bypassing the scheduler's READY queue using C++20 symmetric transfer, and the architectural layers provide complementary perspectives without redundant duplication.
The codebase size budget adheres to the 15KLOC limit across all evaluated components and tiers.

The OS Scheduler design explicitly adopts C++20 coroutine Symmetric Transfer for cooperative context switching (yield/run), minimizing register saving to frame pointer and PC swaps to achieve multi-cycle transition overhead in compliance with {LowOverheadSwitch}.

The design sections for the scheduler strictly adhere to the requirement {COOS_Transparent}. The definition of task state visualization is consistently implemented across the data structure definitions and the internal block diagram.

The audit of the {ConsolidatedHeap} requirement across the provided design sections confirms full vertical and horizontal consistency. The implementation of a single physical pool from which independent partitions are statically carved is consistently described across the system configuration, service policy, and platform memory concept sections. Numeric calculations for the memory budget are accurate and align with the stated constraints.

The audit of {vMMIO_Isolation} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency between the definition and the referencing design sections. The design implements the isolation requirement through a dedicated base address and a controlled page table mechanism.

The audit of {UnifiedAccessModel} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections correctly implement the requirement to unify all physical, logical, and shared memory access through the vMMIO layer to centralize security.

The design sections strictly adhere to the definition of {IPC_HandleBased}. The mechanism of initial URI-based resolution followed by handle-based communication is consistently implemented across the syscall definitions and the IPC router specification.

The design sections for the IPC Router strictly adhere to the definition of {IPCRegistry}. The implementation details regarding the use of fireball::flat_map_view, the O(log N) lookup complexity, and the static nature of the table (constexpr sorted array in ROM) are consistent across the definition and the design documentation.

The audit of {DebuggerLabelTableSwitch} confirms full vertical and horizontal consistency across all referencing design sections. The requirement to switch the interpreter handler table for debugging is consistently implemented as a fallback mechanism that disables JIT and enables step-by-step execution.

The design sections strictly adhere to the definition of {JIT_ReverseCompilationOrder}. The requirement for LIFO processing of the compilation queue to improve immediate chaining is consistently implemented and described across the referencing sections.

The audit of keyword {IPCDI} across the definition and referencing design sections shows full vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections correctly implement the definition's requirement for URI-based dependency resolution and injection.

The referencing design sections are consistent with the definition of {IoC}. The architecture demonstrates the principle through the use of interface realization (dashed lines in BDD) and the explicit implementation of a Service Facade to invert dependencies.
The design sections are vertically and horizontally consistent with the definition of {ConceptHarnessDI}, but there is an unbacked empirical claim regarding performance.

results.summary: The design sections strictly adhere to the definition of {GLOBAL_UseCpp23Library}. The constraints regarding the use of C++23 features and the specific prohibition of std::flat_map in favor of fireball::flat_map_view to avoid std::vector (per {META_NoStdVector}) are consistently maintained across the OS and Scheduler design documents.

The design sections are strictly consistent with the definition of {Challenge_CspHandoffStarvation}. The mitigation strategy (FB_CONF_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_HANDOFFS) is consistently applied across the OS core invariants and the IPC router implementation. Verification claims are properly backed by citations to the formal model.

The referencing design sections are consistent with the definition of {COOS_Scheduling_Refine}. The design implements the 'continuous improvement and optimization' requirement by explicitly deciding on a low-overhead, O(1) round-robin algorithm to eliminate priority-related overheads.

The audit of {Challenge_CoosBlockedList} confirms full consistency between the definition and the referencing design sections. The design decision in ADR-SCHED-003 directly addresses the trade-off between management cost and real-time performance specified in the requirement list.

The referencing design sections are consistent with the definition of {Challenge_DebuggerResource}. The design provides a concrete implementation (FB_CONF_DEBUG_PACKET_SIZE) to address the memory constraint challenge defined in the requirements.

The referencing design sections are consistent with the definition of {WIT_Interface_Purpose}. The definition specifies the requirement for describing the background and logical invariants of the interface design, which is fulfilled by the 'Purpose' section in the WIT interface document and the 'Role' section in the system syscall document.

The audit of {WASI_Async_Bridge} confirms vertical and horizontal consistency across the definition and referencing design sections. The implementation details in the system syscall section correctly expand upon the abstract definition without introducing contradictions.

The design sections strictly adhere to the definition of {Debug_Standard_Env}. The requirement to support VSCode, UART, and J-Link is explicitly mirrored in the design concept, and the functional implementation (attach) provides the necessary mechanism to enable this environment.

The audit of keyword {Wasm32Only} across all referencing design sections confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. All design sections align with the definition's constraints regarding the MVP 32-bit instruction set and the explicit exclusion of floating-point operations and 64-bit extensions.

The design sections strictly adhere to the definition of {ZeroRuntimeOverhead}. The implementation strategy (constexpr DSL for static resolution) directly fulfills the requirement of 'zero-cost abstraction' by shifting computation from runtime to build-time.

The audit of {JIT_ZeroCompileCostTheorem} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections correctly implement the requirement by shifting optimization costs to build-time via a Copy-and-Patch mechanism using pre-compiled stencils.

The referencing design section is consistent with the definition of {LowOverhead}. The design implements the requirement through a specific technical choice (stackless task structure in COOS) to achieve low-overhead switching, which aligns with the definition's goal of minimal resource consumption and low-latency execution.
The referencing design section is vertically consistent with the definition of {ServiceSelfReboot}.
The referencing design section is vertically consistent with the definition of {FaultTolerant}.

The design section strictly adheres to the definition of {SelfReboot_via_Event}. The mechanism is explicitly mapped to the 'TASK_CRASHED' event trigger, fulfilling the requirement for event-driven autonomous service rebooting.

The design section for Heap Partitioning correctly implements and references the IPC_Resource_Isolation requirement. The mechanism for resource isolation (registry management by the IPC router and validation via Generation Cookies) provides a concrete technical implementation of the abstract requirement for 'complete separation and protection' of IPC resources.

The design section strictly adheres to the definition of {EliminateDataRace}. The requirement to eliminate data races via message passing is explicitly implemented in the design through the adoption of Hoare CSP and ownership transfer for zero-copy message passing.

The design section strictly adheres to the definition of {NotRTOS}. The requirement to prioritize memory efficiency and portability over real-time performance is concretely implemented via a stackless green-thread architecture using C++23 coroutines and static allocation, which directly supports the goal of low overhead and memory efficiency.

The design section for the COOS scheduler strictly adheres to the definition of {COOS_Deterministic}. The requirement for deterministic execution via explicit context switch points is correctly mapped to the implementation of a stackless cooperative multitasking system using C++20 symmetric transfer.

The design section strictly adheres to the definition of {WIT_Interface_Spec}. The provided WIT code correctly implements a language-independent interface definition for the 'trap' interface, fulfilling the requirement for a formal interface specification.

The design section strictly adheres to the definition of {Syscall_Return_Value}. The return type (u32), the success/failure convention (0 vs non-zero), and the error propagation mechanism (WASI errno_t to WIT recovery-strategy) are clearly defined and consistent with the requirement for a standard return value and error propagation strategy.

The design implementation for {Challenge_WasiFdWriteLoop} is consistent with its definition. The definition identifies the challenge as 'implementation layer separation and buffer management', and the design section explicitly resolves this by delegating the loop logic to the Shim (guest-side) to keep the host minimal, thereby achieving the required layer separation.
The design section strictly adheres to the definition of the challenge. The mapping between the security gate requirement and the implementation strategy is consistent.

The referencing design section strictly adheres to the definition of {WIT_First}. The design document explicitly establishes the WIT interface as the foundation for system calls and HAL, aligning with the requirement that WIT be the 'sole source of truth' and the starting point of the design.

The referencing design section correctly identifies the requirement {WIT_Common_Types} as a foundational element for the interface specifications. There are no contradictions or inconsistencies between the definition and the design purpose.

The design section for ServiceFacade is vertically consistent with the definition. The definition specifies it as a 'thin wrapper' to hide low-layer IPC and provide type-safe methods, and the design section correctly implements this by stating it 'hides the primitivity of IPC' and enables 'Inversion of Control (IoC)' by allowing the consumer to define the facade class.
The referencing design section is consistent with the definition of {InterpreterContextStackless}.
The design section for vMMIO correctly implements and references the {DynamicMmap} requirement without contradictions or omissions.
The referencing design section is strictly consistent with the definition of {vMMIO_TLB}.
The design conforms to the definition of SinglePassCompilation, but contains an unbacked empirical claim regarding 'Zero Compile Cost'.

results.summary: The referencing design section is consistent with the definition of {HistoryBuffer}.

The audit of {JIT_RegisterMapping} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency across all referencing design sections. The physical register mapping for the ARM Cortex-M33 is consistently defined, and the interaction between the interpreter and JIT trace (including the asymmetric TOS caching) is logically sound and mutually documented.

The audit of {JIT_LazyChaining} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency across all referencing design sections. The implementation details for the chaining mechanism, the physical memory layout of the trace header, and the associated register spill/reload strategy are coherent and logically sound.

The audit of {ADR_SafeQueuingOnHotMiss} confirms full vertical and horizontal consistency across the definition and design sections. The mechanism for preventing double-compilation requests during a 'hot miss' is consistently defined and implemented across the architectural layers.

The audit of {ADR_ScalableCodeOffset} confirms full consistency between the definition and the design implementation. The design section correctly expands upon the definition's goal of determining the representation format for JIT code offsets to handle 32/64-bit boundaries.

The design defines the execution_context and explicitly maps the context base pointer to dedicated physical register R7 on ARM Cortex-M targets, enabling single-cycle base-relative addressing and fulfilling {ContextPointerRegister}.

The audit of {MemoryBoundaryCheck} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency across all referencing design sections. The implementation details in the JIT stencils and interpreter specifications align perfectly with the high-level requirements.

The audit of the {EnvironmentPointer} requirement across all referencing design sections confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The definition of the environment pointer as a type-safe reference to the runtime environment is consistently implemented as the 'env' pointer (vsoc_runtime*) mapped to physical register R2 across the interpreter, JIT compiler, and physical register maps.

The audit of {ADR_TosCacheAsymmetry} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency across all referencing design sections. The asymmetric register convention is consistently applied: the interpreter explicitly avoids TOS caching to preserve R3 as a scratch register, while the JIT utilizes R4/R5 for TOS/NOS caching with a defined, bounded cost (STR x2) during fallback/exit. All register mappings, call signatures, and transition costs are aligned across the architecture, runtime, and JIT compiler specifications.

The audit of the {PositionIndependentCode} requirement across the provided design sections shows full vertical and horizontal consistency. The design implements PIC through a combination of relative addressing, base-relative loads, and a specific relocation strategy for the JIT compiler.

The audit of {META_FlatMapIndexed} across all referencing design sections confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The implementation of the 'flat_map_view' pattern is uniformly applied across JIT entry indexing, vMMIO PTE management, and IPC routing, adhering to the constraints of zero-cost abstraction and the prohibition of std::vector.

The audit of {META_Static_Resolution} across all referencing design sections confirms strict adherence to the definition. The principle of shifting runtime decisions to compile-time to minimize overhead is consistently applied from high-level architecture (Tier 1) down to specific leaf components (Tier 3).

The audit of {LowLatencyJIT} across the provided sections shows high vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections successfully translate the high-level requirement of 'minimizing compile latency' into concrete technical implementations: Copy-and-Patch, Transactional MPU batching, and a specific JIT-Interpreter calling convention. The trade-off regarding TOS/NOS register caching (ADR_TosCacheAsymmetry) is explicitly documented as a bounded cost, preventing a contradiction with the 'Zero-Overhead' claim by redefining the scope of that claim to 'context reconstruction'.

The audit of {GLOBAL_StrictMemoryLimit} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. All numeric allocations sum correctly to the defined budget, and the design sections consistently implement the strict memory constraints through static allocation and bit-packing techniques.

The audit of {META_AccessDictionary} across the provided sections shows strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The keyword is consistently applied to optimize runtime access via indexing (binary search/flat_map) in the IPC Router and WASM Loader, while being explicitly excluded from the bit_view where direct indexing is used instead of search.

The audit of {SimpleJITArchitecture} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The design sections implement the requirement of 'efficient operation within a small JIT cache' through a concrete 3-bank rotating cache and a 3-stage lookup pipeline. Numeric values for cache sizes and memory layouts are consistent across all referencing sections.

The specification for {JIT_MultiBuffer_Cache} is exhaustively consistent across all definition and design sections. Numeric values, architectural roles, and the promotion policy are perfectly aligned.

The audit of {GLOBAL_IdleDetection} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency across the OS core, logging system, and JIT compiler. The definition is consistently implemented as a mechanism for background processing (log flushing and batch compilation) triggered when the system is idle.

The audit of {LowLatencyLookup} confirms strict vertical and horizontal consistency. The requirement for O(log N) lookup via sorted arrays and binary search is uniformly implemented across the TLB design, system containers, and the IPC router. All empirical claims are backed by specific artifact citations.

The audit of {JIT_CopyAndPatch} across definition and design sections shows high vertical and horizontal consistency. The implementation details in the stencil catalog and the compiler orchestration strictly adhere to the 'Copy-and-Patch' definition. Layered perspectives (from high-level runtime state machines to low-level Thumb-2 binary stencils) are correctly applied without redundant duplication of the same abstraction level.

The audit of {META_ZeroCostAbstraction} across all referencing design sections confirms strict adherence to the definition. The implementation patterns (non-owning views, constexpr encoding, and static stencil mapping) consistently align with the goal of eliminating runtime overhead.
